data.summary: Microscopist on 4 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 5 observations; candidates: Actin disruptors, Microtubule stabilizers

observations.finding: Treated fields are sparsely populated with large empty black background vs near-confluent monolayer in DMSO control at same contrast. Fewer cells per field, consistent with growth inhibition / detachment / rounding.

Cell morphology: DMSO shows flat polygonal spread epithelial cells with extended cytoplasm. Treated cells are rounded, contracted, small footprint, often isolated or in small clumps, spiky retraction fibers at edge. Many bright yellow rounded cells.

Actin (red): DMSO shows filamentous stress fibers and continuous cortical actin at cell borders. Treated shows loss of stress fibers; red signal as bright punctate dots primarily at cell periphery, increased heterogeneity / contrast and overall brightness.

Tubulin (green, yellow where overlapping red): DMSO shows radial filamentous microtubule network with moderate intensity. Treated shows compact, very bright diffuse intense staining filling rounded cells, loss of extended filaments, often thick ring-like / bundle appearance, increased brightness and texture.

DNA (blue in composite): DMSO shows single oval uniform blue nuclei of similar size. In treated, blue signal is fainter and often masked by bright yellow cytoplasm; nuclei appear more condensed, irregular outline, occasional bi/multi-lobed or fragmented appearance, no separate grayscale to confirm at high resolution.

notable_cells.why: representative rounded bright yellow cells with peripheral red puncta and loss of spread morphology vs DMSO

candidate_mechanisms.why: Loss of filamentous actin stress fibers, rounding and contraction with peripheral punctate actin aggregates, increased act_mean z=37.3, act_std z=30.0, act_glcm_contrast z=67.5 vs DMSO median 0.002->0.012, and reduced cell_area z=-13.8 (4588->2279 px), as seen in composite red channel.

Marked increase in tubulin intensity and texture (tub_mean z=44.6 0.258->0.711, tub_std z=38.1, tub_glcm_contrast z=44.1) with compact bright diffuse staining and loss of radial filaments, rounded mitotic-like morphology and decreased nuc_solidity z=-20.7 consistent with mitotic arrest/condensed irregular nuclei. Actin change can be secondary to rounding.

report.uncertainty: No separate grayscale DNA/tubulin/actin channels provided; nuclear detail and spindle structure cannot be resolved from composite alone at 1024x819. Both actin and tubulin show very strong increases, so phenotype overlaps actin-disruptor and microtubule-stabilizer classes. Compound identity not inferred; 30 uM, n=271 cells measured, strong deviations |z|>3 in all listed features support described changes.

data.note:
Reflection: Specimen s_5a98540349 was cytochalasin B (PubChem CID 5311281, structure verified; BBBC021 Actin disruptors, no curated ChEMBL mechanism). My blinded conclusion Cholesterol-lowering (p=0.52) followed NSC vote 2/4 and high sim to mevinolin/lovastatin, despite microscopist correctly listing Actin disruptors as top candidate with loss of stress fibers, rounded contracted cells, peripheral punctate actin (act_glcm_contrast z=67.5, act_mean z=37.3, cell_area -13.8) and compact bright tubulin staining.

Failure mode: over-weighting atlas similarity where statins converge on same actin/Rho-dependent morphology via HMG-CoA reductase inhibition -> geranylgeranylation/Rho blockade. Literature shows this convergence: PMIDs 11406567 (RhoA translocation inhibition by statins), 9758637 (geranylgeranylation/Rho role in statin effects). True MoA is actin filament barbed-end capping/disruption: PMID 8781335 directly compares cytochalasin B as microfilament-disrupting agent, and PMIDs 1608453/12686620 discuss actin capping regulation. Dose-responses (tub_mean rho=1.0, act_contrast rho=1.0) and multinucleate proxy were actin-consistent but mis-assigned.

Learn: when microscopist + extreme actin texture + rounding diverge from NSC, prioritize orthogonal imaging phenotype over single-NN vote, especially given known statin-actin crosstalk.

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth: cytochalasin B - actin disruptor. Submitted conclusion Cholesterol-lowering (p=0.52) was incorrect. Verdict correct=false.

What the evidence got right:
- Phenotypic description (e4) explicitly listed Actin disruptors as candidate (with Microtubule stabilizers) based on 4 fields: lower density vs DMSO. This was the only human interpretation and it was correct.
- Feature magnitudes strongly favored actin disruption: well w_7dd5713b24 at 30 uM (e2): act_glcm_contrast z=+67.5, tub_mean z=+44.6, tub_glcm_contrast z=+44.1; well w_b9f2cbcfb2 at 10 uM (e6): act_glcm_contrast z=+36.0, tub_mean z=+27.7. This extreme texture contrast is not typical for cholesterol-lowering alone and is consistent with cytochalasin B as a microfilament-disrupting agent PMID 8781335, which acts via capping/barbed-end inhibition PMID 12686620.
- Cell area reduction and shape change were dose-dependent: w_9c437e9416 1 uM (e3) cell_area z=-8.4, w_f97f19f984 0.3 uM (e7) cell_area z=-7.2; dose_response cell_area rho=-1.00 (e11), nuc_solidity rho=-1.00 (e13), act_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 (e10), tub_mean rho=+1.00 (e9). This contraction/rounding plus texture increase fits actin filament loss.
- Cytokinesis failure signal: frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+8.4 at 1 uM (e3) with dose rho=+0.80 (e12, p=0.2) - classic for actin disruption preventing contractile ring, though p-value was non-significant with only 4 wells and discounted.
- Negative control for MT stabilizer: frac_mitotic_like constant across acquired wells (e14) correctly argued against true mitotic arrest, but we used this only to down-weight Microtubule stabilizers (0.08 in e15) without re-promoting Actin disruptors.

What misled and why:
- compare_to_reference_atlas was the driver of error. At 2 wells (e5): NSC 1/2 Cholesterol-lowering, k-neighbours Microtubule stabilizers 3/10, Cholesterol 2/10, Eg5 2/10. At 4 wells (e8): NSC 2/4 Cholesterol-lowering, k-neighbours Protein synthesis 4/10, Cholesterol 2/10, Eg5 2/10. We updated hypotheses (e15) to Cholesterol 0.52 vs Actin 0.22 based on e8+e2+e6+e9+e10+e11, explicitly listing e4 as contradicting but still outvoted by computation.
- The cholesterol class mimics actin morphology because HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors alter RhoA translocation/prenylation and geranylgeranylation-dependent cytoskeletal organization PMID 11406567 PMID 9758637 PMID 16929252. That explains why atlas neighbours with high actin/tub contrast map to Cholesterol-lowering, but we did not interrogate this confound during the run; literature search for this was only post-hoc (e20).
- Acquisition choices amplified the misclassification: we sampled only one replicate per dose (30, 1, 10, 0.3 uM - e2, e3, e6, e7) of 8 available doses, no replicates, and relied on 4-point dose_response with perfect rho values (e9,e10,e11) to claim dose-dependence without testing an orthogonal actin readout. High-dose saturation (271 cells at 30 uM vs 360 at 1 uM, e2 vs e3) with very high tub_std z=+23.0 (e6) also introduced toxicity/stress texture that pushed k-neighbours to Protein synthesis (e8), which we failed to recognize as high-dose artifact rather than MoA signal.
- We over-weighted tub_mean increase (z=+44.6) as potential stabilizer/cholesterol signal and under-weighted that tub increase accompanies cell rounding after actin loss, and we ignored that cell_nuc_area_ratio z=-5.0 (e7) supports cytoplasmic contraction.

Missed opportunity: Actin disruptors had supporting e2,e4,e6 but contradicting e8 per e15, and was left at 0.22. With microscopist + extreme act_glcm_contrast + multinucleate proxy + negative mitotic signal, the prior for Actin should have remained >Cholesterol, and atlas vote of 2/4 with diverse k-neighbours should have been treated as low-confidence. Post-unblinding lookup (e17,e18) confirms name and BBBC021 structure agree for cytochalasin B (CID 5311281) with no curated mechanism to rely on, so morphology had to be decisive - we chose the computational vote over the visual phenotype.

This is phenotypic screening data only; no clinical interpretation is made.

## Reflection

- Phenotypic description (e4) explicitly listed Actin disruptors as candidate (with Microtubule stabilizers) based on 4 fields: lower density vs DMSO. This was the only human interpretation and it was correct.

- Cytokinesis failure signal: frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+8.4 at 1 uM (e3) with dose rho=+0.80 (e12, p=0.2) - classic for actin disruption preventing contractile ring, though p-value was non-significant with only 4 wells and discounted.
- Negative control for MT stabilizer: frac_mitotic_like constant across acquired wells (e14) correctly argued against true mitotic arrest, but we used this only to down-weight Microtubule stabilizers (0.08 in e15) without re-promoting Actin disruptors.

What misled and why:
- compare_to_reference_atlas was the driver of error. At 2 wells (e5): NSC 1/2 Cholesterol-lowering, k-neighbours Microtubule stabilizers 3/10, Cholesterol 2/10, Eg5 2/10. At 4 wells (e8): NSC 2/4 Cholesterol-lowering, k-neighbours Protein synthesis 4/10, Cholesterol 2/10, Eg5 2/10. We updated hypotheses (e15) to Cholesterol 0.52 vs Actin 0.22 based on e8+e2+e6+e9+e10+e11, explicitly listing e4 as contradicting but still outvoted by computation.
- The cholesterol class mimics actin morphology because HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors alter RhoA translocation/prenylation and geranylgeranylation-dependent cytoskeletal organization PMID 11406567 PMID 9758637 PMID 16929252. That explains why atlas neighbours with high actin/tub contrast map to Cholesterol-lowering, but we did not interrogate this confound during the run; literature search for this was only post-hoc (e20).
- Acquisition choices amplified the misclassification: we sampled only one replicate per dose (30, 1, 10, 0.3 uM - e2, e3, e6, e7) of 8 available doses, no replicates, and relied on 4-point dose_response with perfect rho values (e9,e10,e11) to claim dose-dependence without testing an orthogonal actin readout.
